title: Apple Pay Eyes India Launch Next Month, Starting With Axis Bank Cards
excerpt: Reuters reports Apple is poised to bring its tap-and-pay service to one of the last major markets where it is unavailable, with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank also in talks but yet to agree terms.
body:
• Apple is poised to launch Apple Pay in India as early as next month, with Axis Bank's credit cards first in line, three sources told Reuters.
  • HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are in talks but have yet to agree on commercial terms; Apple plans to add lenders bank-by-bank over time.
  • The launch caps a nearly decade-long effort that began in 2017, stalled by data-localisation rules and UPI integration hurdles — both now largely resolved.
  • Apple enters a market where UPI handles 84% of digital payments, betting that tokenised, biometric card payments can win over its growing iPhone user base.

A decade in the making

Apple is poised to launch Apple Pay in India as early as next month with Axis Bank's credit cards, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Friday, in what would finally bring the company's payments service to one of the few major economies where it remains unavailable. Mumbai-based Axis Bank, India's fourth-largest credit card issuer, would be the launch partner, with Apple adding more lenders over time through direct, bank-by-bank deals — the same phased approach it has used in other markets.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=lQzY6vXLgRk

The company has also held discussions with Axis Bank's larger private-sector rivals HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, two of the sources said, but neither has yet agreed on commercial terms. Apple and HDFC did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment; ICICI and Axis declined to comment.

The timing marks the culmination of a nearly decade-long push. Apple first signalled plans to launch Apple Pay in India in 2017, but the rollout ran into regulatory and technical hurdles, including India's data-localisation requirements and the challenge of integrating with the country's homegrown Unified Payments Interface. A Bloomberg report in February indicated Apple was aiming for a launch around the middle of 2026, possibly with UPI support alongside card payments.

Why now

Two developments have cleared the path. Last year, the Reserve Bank of India permitted alternative authentication mechanisms — including biometrics — for card payments, which allows services like Apple Pay to authenticate Indian bank-card transactions through Face ID or Touch ID. Meanwhile, Apple's footprint in the country has grown sharply: its share of India's smartphone market has doubled to 8% since 2022, according to Counterpoint Research, making India one of Apple's most important growth markets.

Apple Pay lets iPhone and Apple Watch users make contactless purchases using tokenised card details stored on the device, authenticated by Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode, without opening a separate payments app. Axis Bank had around 16.26 million active credit cards in circulation as of July, per RBI data, trailing HDFC Bank, SBI Cards and ICICI Bank — though Apple's addressable base will initially be limited to iPhone owners holding cards from participating banks.

The uphill climb

The biggest question is how much room exists for a card-based service in a market UPI has conquered. UPI accounts for roughly 84% of India's digital payment volumes, and NPCI's UPI Tap & Pay already lets users tap NFC-enabled phones at compatible terminals — though those transactions run through the UPI network rather than a card's rails. Apple has also held discussions with Mastercard and Visa, according to earlier reports, with friction over how to split fees: Apple has reportedly sought a 15-20 basis-point share of the interchange fee on its transactions, while some banks have countered with around 10 basis points.

For Apple, the commercial stakes go beyond payments revenue. Apple Pay deepens the ecosystem lock-in that drives iPhone upgrades and services growth in a market where premium smartphones are still gaining share. For Indian banks, the calculus is whether access to Apple's growing — and affluent — user base justifies conceding a slice of interchange income in a business already under margin pressure from zero-MDR UPI transactions.

What it means for NRIs

For the diaspora, an India Apple Pay launch is most immediately useful on visits home: NRIs carrying iPhones with Indian bank cards will be able to tap-to-pay at India's growing network of contactless terminals without carrying physical cards or juggling UPI apps tied to Indian mobile numbers. Longer term, if Apple Pay eventually supports UPI — as earlier reports suggested — it could become the first genuinely global wallet with native access to India's real-time payments network.

What to watch

The launch date remains sourced, not official — Apple has said nothing publicly, and commercial terms with HDFC and ICICI are still unresolved. Watch for which bank signs next, whether UPI rails are included at launch, and how aggressively NPCI and Indian banks respond in a market they currently dominate.
